title: Does a cheap rung's rank correlation with the expensive rung predict how well it works as a top-k screen?
summary: The eda projects judge cheap proxies by Spearman rank correlation with the SKY130-mapped objective, but a search loop only uses the top of the proxy's list. Over 207 screens of the 40 MAC-engine designs of eda-sky130rung (7 named proxies from eda-delayproxy and 200 random re-weightings of its logical-effort delay; Yosys 0.33, ABC dc2; map, SKY130 HD), agreement predicts payoff only when the screens already rank well. For mapped area × latency, across screens Spearman agreement and the chance that the pool's best design is among the first mapped correlate at 0.60 (bootstrap 0.50 to 0.68). For mapped latency alone they do not (−0.13, −0.26 to 0.02): the highest-Spearman screen (0.958) maps the best design first only 0.324 of the time, while gate count, at Spearman 0.551, does so 0.692, and 14 of 175 screens with Spearman ≥ 0.9 do not put the true best in their top 3. The best design's rank in the screen's order predicts payoff (0.90 for latency) but a loop cannot compute it without the mapping. The area × latency screens reproduce eda-latencyhalve's 0.636 and 0.970. Preliminary: one design family, one ABC script, no place and route; the swept screens are correlated variants of one model, so the bootstrap over screens is optimistic.
lede: across 207 cheap screens of 40 MAC engines, Spearman agreement with SKY130-mapped latency does not predict top-k screening payoff (−0.13 at k = 1): the highest-Spearman screen (0.958) maps the best design first 32% of the time, gate count (0.551) 69%; for area × latency it does (0.60).
